### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **54** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**59** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 61e5ee9e5720433ccca483160bccbf880e6d9b84`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **34** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 61e5ee9e5720433ccca483160bccbf880e6d9b84` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dce801dfa5347e5949e62a7dadbe00be088460c2` — the merge of head `f588d6631992c93ef870fbe53571d3f94fa5e56c` into base `61e5ee9e5720433ccca483160bccbf880e6d9b84`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dce801dfa5347e5949e62a7dadbe00be088460c2 && git checkout dce801dfa5347e5949e62a7dadbe00be088460c2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 61e5ee9e5720433ccca483160bccbf880e6d9b84 f588d6631992c93ef870fbe53571d3f94fa5e56c && git checkout -B drift-repro 61e5ee9e5720433ccca483160bccbf880e6d9b84 && git merge --no-ff f588d6631992c93ef870fbe53571d3f94fa5e56c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 61e5ee9e5720433ccca483160bccbf880e6d9b84
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 61e5ee9e5720433ccca483160bccbf880e6d9b84` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `e499adaf65d76630508f92b4cd65ad3d73155acc`
Local-runs: none

Rendered at `TIER_DEFAULT`. The face is the `Clause-②: yes` declaration: there is no `packages/spec/src/**` path, and `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 23881` reads 0 of 23 paths on the register (2,276 changed lines, under 3,000). The head is the one the brief named (`e499adaf65`, resolved in full above).

Read in this act:
- card #23857's body and both comments (the claim `6212515645`, the dev's report `6214364566`);
- the parent card #23732's body and all 10 comments: the scratch readings and release `6206614195`, the director's delta `6211484740` and the ruling `6212058353`;
- PR #23881's body, its 23-path file list, its one comment (the docs-drift bot) and its net diff against `main` (merge base `34b740f2d`);
- the 41 check-runs on the head, latest per name;
- E6's contract record `6209058891` on PR #23814. This record follows its ① items in kind.

Scope: every path of the code diff.
- In `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/`: `objects/sys-comment.object.ts`, `comment-access-hooks.ts`, `comment-parent-pair-backfill.ts`, `audit-plugin.ts`, `index.ts`, the four generated translations and the two new suites.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/comment-parent-pair.ts`, with its suite and its three family registrations.
- The dogfood pin.

Read on `origin/main` at `497518c3f6`. Of these paths, only `audit-writers.ts` moved after the merge base, and its `SKIP_OBJECTS` set is byte-identical:
- `parent-record-read-gate.ts`: `enumerateParentObjects`, `planParentReads`, `hasObjectAdmission`, `computeParentRecordFilter`, `WHOLE_READ_PROBE_WHY`;
- `audit-writers.ts`: `SKIP_OBJECTS` and `AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS`;
- `objectql/src/engine.ts`: `hasObjectMiddleware`, `composeReadableIdsAtBoundary`, `refuseUncomposableReadableIdsClasses`, and on the update path the hook-view hide and the static strip;
- `objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts`: `staticReadonlyInsertSubject`, `stripReadonlyFields`, `isPreservableUnderAudit`;
- `core/src/utils/import-runner.ts` and `rest/src/import-prepare.ts` (the historical-import write context), and `rest/src/rest-server.ts#enforceApiAccess`;
- every global `registerMiddleware` call outside the tests;
- E6's shape: `activity-changed-fields-backfill.ts` and `migrate/activity-changed-fields.ts`;
- ADR-0139 (`docs/adr/0139-engine-internal-semi-join-leaf-readable-parent-ids.md`) D2 to D5 and D5.2, and ADR-0052 §5;
- `scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs` (the declaration rule).

The changeset's prose and the docs are the lane seat's ACCEPT, except the changeset's `Clause-②:` line and level, which ② judges. Stamp of this act: 2026-10-16T12:01Z.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The two columns on the platform object `sys_comment`: right.**
  - `object_name` and `record_id` are `Field.text`, `readonly`, not required, `maxLength` 255 each, in the `Thread` group. 255 is the thread's own bound, so no stamped part can exceed it. They use ADR-0052 §5's names.
  - They are indexed together as `(object_name, record_id)`. The leaf (one `record_id IN` per `object_name`) and the probe (`object_name IS NULL`) both read through that index's prefix.
  - They are served to every reader of the row, with no redaction and no query-guard entry. That is right. The pair is a parse of `thread_id`, which every reader of the row is already served and may filter by. A `sys_comment` row carries no parent field value, so this stream withholds no parent field from any reader, and a predicate on the pair tests only what the row already shows.
  - No permission set in tree narrows `sys_comment` by field.

- **The writer cannot set the pair: wrong on the update side.**
  - **Create: right.** `installCommentParentPairStamp`'s `beforeInsert` (`comment-access-hooks.ts:345`) writes the planner's pair over any value sent, for every caller, SYSTEM included, on a single row or a batch. The create-side readonly strip returns no subject for a `sys_` object (`staticReadonlyInsertSubject`), so that write is the guard, as it is for `is_edited`. Pinned: a SYSTEM insert that sent the vault pair and a member insert that sent the vault pair both read back the thread's pair (ablation A6).
  - **The re-point: right.** An update that names `thread_id` is re-stamped (`:362`), and the hook's value survives the strip through `hookWrittenKeys` (pinned; A7).
  - **The gap.** An update that names the pair without `thread_id` runs no stamp. The head relies on the engine's update-side strip to drop a non-system caller's value.
  - **That strip has an exemption.** Under `preserveAudit` it keeps every readonly field `isPreservableUnderAudit` admits (`rule-validator.ts:2781`: any field not marked `system: true`). That holds both in the hook view (the update path's `stripReadonlyFields` call with `preserveAudit`, at the hide) and at the static strip.
  - **`preserveAudit` reaches ordinary callers.** The REST import's `treatAsHistorical: true` (`import-prepare.ts:301`) puts `preserveAudit: true` on the write context of every row it updates (`import-runner.ts:766`), for any caller the import door admits. `sys_comment` declares no `apiMethods`, so `enforceApiAccess` admits `import`, and the comment update gate admits the comment's author or the parent's editor.
  - **What follows, by source reading at this head** (not measured; this review runs nothing). The author of a comment on record X can import-update its `object_name` / `record_id` to any record Y, including one they cannot read, while `thread_id` still names X. The leaf authorizes by the pair. So Y's readers are then served the comment on every broad read and on every read filtered by the pair, and X's readers no longer see it.
  - **Why that matters.** It is the planting on an unreadable record that the re-point rule ("Cannot move comment to … you cannot read it") exists to refuse, and a parent's editor can do it to other people's comments.
  - **What it contradicts:** ruling item 1 ("read-only to authors"); the object docblock ("a non-system update's own value is stripped by the engine"); the changeset's "a non-system caller's own value for either column is dropped by the engine on update". The pin that covers the strip (`the re-point rule re-stamps the pair; a member's own pair is never written`) sends no `preserveAudit`. **FAIL reason 1.**
  - **The fix.** The engine's own docblock on `isPreservableUnderAudit` names the class of fix: a historical import "must not forge tenancy or system-generated values", and the pair is a system-generated value that authorizes reads. Either fix closes the gap:
    - declare both fields `system: true`, so the strip removes them under `preserveAudit` too, with SYSTEM still exempt; or
    - have the update stamp re-derive or drop the pair whenever an update names either column.

- **The read rule, against ruling items 1–5: right.**
  - **One `ReadableIds` leaf per registered parent object, over the pair.** `computeThreadVisibilityFilter` (`:1162`) calls E5's `computeParentRecordFilter` with `commentThreadGate()` (`:1069`): `{ object: 'sys_comment', denyAll: READ_DENY_ALL, namedParents: [...AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS] }`, with no outside class and no exemption. Each composable parent P gets `{ object_name: P, record_id: { $in: ReadableIds.of(P) } }`, ORed together and ANDed into the read's WHERE on `find`, `findOne`, `count` and `aggregate`.
  - **No pre-scan, and no SYSTEM-composed read or leaf.** No pre-scan reads the stamped rows on composable parents. The only SYSTEM reads left are the two the ruling keeps: D5's pair probe (`object_name $in` the probed parents) and the thread probe of unstamped rows. Neither carries a leaf, because both read the caller's WHERE before the gate ANDs its own filter in. Pinned on the real stack by the dogfood's census of SYSTEM reads.
  - **D5's classes and the two whole-read states, chosen up front.** Before any branch is written, `planParentReads` decides from the context, the registry and the bindings among: a delegated caller, an object-scoped middleware (`hasObjectMiddleware`), a federated parent, `engine-cannot-classify` and `no-object-admission`. Pinned per class (A8b, A9).
  - **No leaf without `canReadObject`.** `hasObjectAdmission` sends the whole read to the probe, and `AuditPlugin` now passes the security source to the installer (A4).
  - **The consumer catches nothing (D3).** The gate's `try` wraps only its own filter computation, and `next()` sits outside it (`:1055`). Pinned on a driver that refuses the leaf (D3's envelope, never the sentinel) and by A5.
  - **An unstamped row is probed, never leafed.** A leaf branch requires `object_name = P`, which a NULL never satisfies. The probe pre-scans the caller's WHERE AND `object_name IS NULL`, and emits `{ object_name: NULL, thread_id: { $in: VISIBLE } }`, so it can select no stamped row (A2, A3). A thread that names no record keeps `null` / `null`: that probe scans it on every read and never adds it to the list, so it stays hidden, as before.
  - **The reaction gate is unchanged (D5.2).** `computeReactionVisibilityFilter` is byte-identical. Its caller-scoped read of `sys_comment` now meets the leafed comment gate, which narrows it exactly as it narrows a direct comment read. Pinned: the emitted WHERE is a literal `comment_id` list.
  - **Probe failures fail closed.** If the pair probe fails, the stamped rows get the deny-all sentinel and the gate says so; if the unstamped probe fails, the whole read is denied.

- **The parent set (the dev's Q1, A taken): right.**
  - **What it enumerates.** `namedParents: [...AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS]` takes all 21 `SKIP_OBJECTS` entries out of `enumerateParentObjects`'s exclusion. The `name === gate.object` test still keeps `sys_comment` out. So the gate enumerates every registered machine-named object except `sys_comment`, which is the registered part of what `parseCommentThreadId` accepts (it refuses `sys_comment` itself).
  - **It preserves exactly what the old gate served:**
    - An unregistered object gets no leaf and no row; the old probe found no readable id for it either.
    - `sys_activity` and `sys_audit_log`, newly named, carry object-scoped read middleware. They fall in D5.2 and keep the old mechanism itself.
    - For the other named parents, the leaf is D2's composition from `canReadObject` and `getReadFilter`, which the ADR holds equal to a direct read. I found no narrowing of their reads outside those two. Every global `registerMiddleware` on `main` outside the tests is a write-side or post-write hook: plugin-auth's two, the organizations plugin's three, the app plugin's seed handoff, plugin-security's bootstrap replay and `sys_member` reconciler, plugin-sharing's `sys_organization` trigger, and the verify harness's write observer. plugin-security's CRUD middleware and plugin-sharing's `'*'` read scope are the scope D2 holds `getReadFilter` to answer.
  - **It opens nothing.** No object becomes readable that was not before. B would have hidden, silently, the comments the old gate served on `sys_job`, `sys_session` and the rest.
  - **The cost per unpinned read.** It is the activity gate's branch set plus up to 18 more: 20 named parents, minus the two D5.2 ones.
    - Each leaf is composed per driver call (`find` and `count` each), with one `canReadObject` and, for an admitted object, one `getReadFilter`, nothing memoised. A refused object is answered `$in: []`, with no subquery.
    - Every non-system comment read also runs the unstamped probe: one indexed SYSTEM `find`, which after the backfill finds only the threads that name no record.
    - It also runs the pair probe whenever a D5.2 or federated parent is registered.
    - The gate does not narrow by a pinned parent, so the read of a record's own thread (the console's reader) pays the same as a broad read.
    - The PR body names this as E5's cost class. It is not measured on an app-sized registry or table.

- **The exported backfill and its door: right.**
  - **E6's shape.** `backfillCommentParentPair(engine, logger, { apply, pageSize })` matches E6's `backfillActivityChangedFields` one for one. It runs a SYSTEM `find` over `object_name $null`, pages by `id` ascending (500 rows a page), projects `id, thread_id, updated_at`, and makes a single-id SYSTEM update of both columns.
  - **`preserveAudit` keeps `updated_at`.** The update runs under `preserveAudit` with the stored `updated_at`, so the row keeps its timestamp (pinned through the door, case 2). It names no `thread_id` and no `body`, so it causes no re-point and no edit stamp, and `sys_comment` is outside the audit writer.
  - **Dry run by default, and idempotent.** A stamped row leaves the set; an unparented row stays and is counted; the cursor moves past both. Pinned: a second `--apply` stamps 0.
  - **A refused page read exits 1.** The read is counted and the walk stops, so the door exits 1 (pinned; A10b).
  - **The door** differs from `migrate/activity-changed-fields.ts` only in names and prose. It has the same five flags, the same read-only dry-run boot with `absentTableReads`, and the same exit 1 when `failures` is above 0. It is registered in the one-shot family table, the JSON-purity family and the absent-database roster.

- **No third copy of the D5 classification: right.** `comment-access-hooks.ts` imports `computeParentRecordFilter`, and `parent-record-read-gate.ts` is not on the file list. The unstamped-row probe is the gate's pre-E7 thread probe, restricted to unstamped rows. It does no classification.

- **The ADR anchors: right.**
  - ADR-0139's two anchors into a touched file still resolve under the resolver's declaration rule:
    - `comment-access-hooks.ts#installCommentReadVisibility` is an `export function` at `:1017`, the installer the consumer row names;
    - `#READ_SCAN_LIMIT` is the same `const` binding, unchanged, and is still the thread probe's bound.
  - No other ADR and no `scripts/adr-anchors/` entry points into a touched file, and no `docs/adr/**` path is on the list.
  - The dev's local `check:adr-symbol-anchors` run (2,348 anchors across 142 records) agrees, and `Lint & Repo Gates` is `success`. Neither is cited as the judgment.

- **The public surface: right in kind.**
  - New package exports: `backfillCommentParentPair`, `COMMENT_PARENT_PAIR_BACKFILL_PAGE_SIZE`, the backfill's engine and report types, `planCommentParentPair`, `COMMENT_PARENT_OBJECT_COLUMN`, `COMMENT_PARENT_RECORD_COLUMN` and `CommentParentPair`.
  - `installCommentReadVisibility` takes an optional third argument. Its first parameter is now `ParentRecordGateEngine` (`CommentAccessEngine` plus three optional members). That brings `ParentRecordGateEngine` and `ParentObjectReadAdmissionSource`, types `index.ts` does not export, into the published declaration's reach.
  - `CommentAccessEngine` gains an optional `getSchema`.
  - All of these widen; nothing is removed or narrowed. `commentThreadGate`, `declaresCommentParentPair` and `COMMENT_PARENT_PAIR_COLUMNS` are module exports that `index.ts` does not re-export.

- **The derived gate families on this head: right.**
  - All 41 check-runs (latest per name) completed: 36 `success`, 5 `skipped`, 0 failure, 0 pending. The skipped five are opt-in or excluded on `pull_request` by `ci.yml`: Console Pin Gate, the dogfood matrix shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, the packed-tarball smoke and Temporal Conformance.
  - The successes include all six `Test Core` shards, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check.
  - No PR check runs the dogfood pin; the dev's run is its measurement of record.

- **Observations, not reasons (the lane's call; by my reading, (a) to (c) belong in the patch round):**
  - (a) **A race in the backfill.** The backfill reads a page, then writes each row's pair by id, with no condition on the write. If a re-point lands between the read and that row's write, the pair keeps naming the thread the comment left, and the backfill never revisits the row because it is no longer unstamped. Either fix closes it:
    - a compare-and-set write, whose `where` also requires `object_name` null and the `thread_id` the page read; or
    - a pair derived from the row's own thread at write time, which also closes FAIL reason 1 if the update stamp re-derives the pair whenever an update names it.
  - (b) The changeset names the optional third argument, but not the first parameter's wider type or the two types it brings into reach (see ②).
  - (c) The door's docblock says its flags are "`os migrate comment-parent-pair`'s, one for one". It means `activity-changed-fields`'s.
  - (d) The cost in the Q1 item is not measured at app scale.

### ② Semver level

- **The level: right.** `minor` for `@objectstack/plugin-audit` and `@objectstack/cli` matches what the diff publishes: two columns and an index on a published platform object, new package exports, a wider installer signature and a new CLI subcommand, with nothing removed.
- **The `Clause-②:` line: right.** `Clause-②: yes` is on the PR body's line 2 and in the changeset body, with no arm, and `yes` takes at least `minor`. The change is not breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition is owed.
- **The `driver-mongodb` 500.** It is ADR-0139 D3's ruled consequence (O3). The changeset states it, as E5's and the attachment card's did.
- **Ruling item 2 (the first paragraph): right.** It binds the changeset's FIRST paragraph, which carries the whole of it in #23731's form:
  - "Run `os migrate comment-parent-pair --apply` at once after upgrading";
  - the rollout consequence: until it runs, rows written before the upgrade are answered by the bounded 2,000-row probe, so a broad list can omit visible comments with a `total` that agrees, and a record's own thread is unaffected;
  - the door: a dry run by default, `--apply` to write, idempotent, both columns in one run, `updated_at` kept, and E6's flags one for one;
  - the measured difference: a dry run against a database not yet synced exits 1.
- `Check Changeset` is green.
- **One sentence of the third paragraph is false at this head**: "a non-system caller's own value for either column is dropped by the engine on update" (FAIL reason 1). The fix makes it true, or the patch round rewords it. Observation (b) above is prose for the same round.
- `packages/qa/dogfood` is not a released package.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Q1 (the parent set): A, right** (see ① above). It preserves what the old gate served and opens nothing, and B would be the silent narrowing the ruling's floor forbids. The cost is E5's class and is named in the PR body. If that cost ever matters, narrowing by a pinned parent is a later card for #22788, the owner of `parent-record-read-gate.ts`, not for this card.
- **Q2 (the comments checklist item): A, right.** No item covers comment read inheritance. The platform checklist's one comment item, `records-forms.record-discussion-mentions`, is about posting and the feed. Revising `attachments-storage.read-inherits-parent-rls` (revision 5, with the two notes from `6206614195`) and recording that no comments item exists is the honest route. Authoring a comments read-inheritance item is work for a `checklist-author` sweep. It is escalated to the seat, which may order one; this review files nothing.
- **Deviation 1 (docs and regenerated files outside the claim's list): accepted**, as in E6. The files are `deployment/cli.mdx`, `platform-checklist/areas/cli.json` (17 to 18), the tenant-audit census (226 to 227 sites, the new one being the backfill's update, with the prose figures edited by hand) and the checklist item that ruling item 6 assigns to this card.
- **Deviation 2: right.** The stamp and the gate live in `comment-access-hooks.ts`, the backfill in its own module, and `audit-writers.ts` is only imported, not edited. That is inside the claim's "or one new module beside it" and clear of #23804's `writeAudit`, which has since landed on `main` with `SKIP_OBJECTS` unchanged.
- **Deviation 3: right.** `parent-record-read-gate.ts` is imported, not edited, and the file is not on the list. A8b and A9 mutated it temporarily, and each restore was proven blob-identical.
- **Deviation 4: right, and the right call.** The first dogfood fixture passed under A0, so the dev rebuilt it with one comment per record. The old probe bounded distinct threads, so only a fixture past the window in threads measures it, and the first green is not counted.
- **Deviations 5–10: process notes consistent with AGENTS.md; nothing to answer.** They are: a bundled lock call, with each part's exit quoted; one refused `rm` of a fixture directory the suites do not read; the JSON-purity e2e run before the main merge; the detached primary checkout; the model-free trailer pair; and one `subscribe_pr_activity` call, which is no GitHub write.
- **The out-of-scope finding (`WHOLE_READ_PROBE_WHY['no-object-admission']` stale prose; carrier #22788): right, noted and not filed.** The sentence still cites "the SYSTEM re-read of this WHERE that the withheld-update rule makes", which E6 removed, and the comment seam now prints it once per engine when no `canReadObject` is composed. Only the prose is wrong; the behaviour is right. The file is excluded from this card and belongs to #22788 (open, `domain:engine`); the seat carries the note there.
- **The readings are the dev's, not this record's.** These are the dev's local measurements, with A0 as the before-leg; this record ran none of them:
  - the bound case on a real engine: member 1,766 to 2,303 of 2,303, administrator `total` 2,000 to 2,605;
  - the bound case on the real stack at the HTTP door: member 981 to 2,050 of 2,050;
  - the reaction reading, recorded as D5.2's class: member 1,763 of 2,300, administrator 2,000 of 2,601.

Implemented-by: `session_01NX4Woa8XhvMs6xpqQpx8kK`
Reviewed-by: `session_018VqJPGA1NDNSCZsnecsChP`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

FAIL reason, against the diff at this head:
1. **A non-system caller can write the pair on update.** An update that names `object_name` / `record_id` without `thread_id` runs no stamp. Under `preserveAudit`, which the REST import's `treatAsHistorical: true` puts on an ordinary caller's write, the engine's update-side readonly strip keeps both values, because neither field is marked `system: true` (`isPreservableUnderAudit`). The leaf authorizes by the pair. So a comment's author, or its parent's editor, can point the comment at any record, including one they cannot read, while its thread still names the first.
